title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Standards, Prompt Sets, Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization & Regression Playbook
author: Priya Shenoy
content:
Summary

This page codifies Redwood Inference’s applied-ML evaluation (eval) harness standards, onboarding checklist for new models, prompt set and benchmark guidelines, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and a regression triage playbook. It is intended for ML engineers, model-onboarding owners, SREs who run periodic evaluations, and product engineers who rely on model quality metrics for rollout decisions.

Purpose and scope
- Provide a single, opinionated reference for designing and running automated evals across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Cover the lifecycle: model onboarding -> baseline evaluations -> quantization validation -> canary/regression monitoring -> triage and rollback.
- Targeted workloads: chat completion, instruction-following, summarization, code generation, classification, and embeddings.

Principles
1) Reproducibility: every eval must be versioned (model, prompt set, harness config) and executable via CI.
2) Coverage-first: test across distribution slices (short/long context, domain shift, instruction variety).
3) Signal prioritization: prioritize actionable metrics (accuracy/intent match, hallucination rate, safety violations, latency/regression delta).
4) Fast feedback: nightly baseline runs + per-change smoke tests in PRs.
5) Guardrail alignment: tie eval thresholds to deployment policies (canary, auto-rollout, manual gates).

Eval harness architecture (high level)
- Components:
  - runner: orchestrates tasks, retries, parallelizes across workers.
  - dataset manager: versioned prompt sets and annotations (stored in S3/GCS + manifest).
  - metrics service: aggregates model outputs and computes metrics (similarity, BLEU/ROUGE, exact match, embedding drift).
  - comparison engine: diff/paired-run analysis for regression detection.
  - reporting: per-model summary, change summaries, charts, and alert hooks into Slack or PagerDuty.

Onboarding checklist (for a new model/version)
1) Metadata: add model entry to model registry with name, architecture, size, quantization support, expected sequence lengths, recommended batch sizes, and owner.
2) Baseline dataset selection:
   - Select 3 canonical prompt sets (general-purpose, domain-specific, failure-mode).
   - Include at least 1 adversarial prompt set (to probe hallucination) and 1 safety prompt set.
3) CI integration:
   - Add a PR smoke test (5-20 prompts) that runs in <5m.
   - Add nightly full-run job (target completion <4h for typical models; adjust for very large models).
4) Metric mapping: define primary/secondary metrics and thresholds (see metric table below).
5) Latency & resource profile: run perf harness to collect p50/p95 token latency and cost estimates on target deployment tier.
6) Quantization matrix: list supported quantization formats (FP16, int8, awq, gptq) and mark which profile is recommended for production.
7) Release policy: define canary rollout steps (10%, 50%, 100%) with minimum pass criteria at each stage.
8) Documentation: link this model to the prompt-set documentation and evaluation dashboards.

Standard prompt sets and benchmark guidelines
- Prompt set types (minimum required):
  - Canonical usage: common production prompts reflecting customer usage.
  - Edge / long-context: prompts with long context windows to test memory/KV behavior.
  - Safety & toxicity: curated set to check content policy violations.
  - Hallucination probes: fact-checking questions and grounding tests.
  - Instruction fidelity: complex multi-step instructions.
  - Domain-specific sets: finance, healthcare, legal (when applicable).
- Prompt set versioning: each set must include a manifest.json with fields: id, version, description, license, source, split (train/val/test), and intended metric mapping.
- Benchmarks:
  - Use a mixture of open benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, GSM8K as appropriate) and internal production datasets.
  - Do not depend exclusively on aggregate single-number scores; always include slice-level breakdowns.

Metric definitions and thresholds (recommended defaults)
| Metric | Definition | Typical threshold | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Accuracy / EM | Exact match or task-specific accuracy | >= baseline_model - 2% | Baselines are model-family specific |
| Intent-match | Human or classifier judgment that output fulfills task | >= 90% | Use automatic classifiers for nightly; human evals monthly |
| Hallucination rate | Fraction of outputs with fabricated assertions | <= 5% for general models | Domain-sensitive; lower for factual assistants |
| Safety violations | Policy violations flagged by classifier | <= 1% | Immediate fail for public deployment >1% |
| Latency p95 (token) | 95th percentile token-generation latency | < 150ms token at target tier | Varies by deployment tier |
| Regression delta | Relative change vs baseline on key metrics | <= 1.5% negative change | Triggers triage if exceeded |

Quality guardrails and checks
- Automated checks (run in CI/nightly):
  1) Deterministic smoke: seed-based reproducibility for sampling configs.
  2) Safety scan: run safety classifier; fail on >1% violations for public models.
  3) Hallucination probe: run fact-checker; block if hallucination rate increases >1.5x baseline.
  4) Latency check: compare p95/p50 to baseline; block if p95 exceeds baseline by >20%.
  5) Embedding drift: compare mean cosine similarity vs baseline on canonical set; alert if mean drops by >0.05.
- Human-in-the-loop checks:
  - Monthly human eval on sample of 500 outputs for production models; include multi-rater adjudication for contentious examples.

Quantization profile guidance
- Profiles: each profile must be documented with: name, quantization method, supported layers, expected density of errors, recommended use-cases. Example profiles: fp16, int8-ptq, gptq-4bit, awq-4bit.
- Validation steps for any quantized build:
  1) Unit tests: layerwise numeric comparison to FP16 baseline (max per-layer abs error thresholds).
  2) End-to-end eval: run canonical prompt sets and ensure primary metrics within reg threshold (see metric table).
  3) Perf/Limits: run memory and throughput tests, document p95 latency and tokens/sec.
  4) Fallback config: include server-side automatic fallback to higher-precision variant if quality regressions detected at runtime.
- Quantization decision matrix:
  - Use int8/gptq for bulk cost-sensitive workloads where regression delta <1% and hallucination is stable.
  - Use 4-bit profiles (awq/gptq) for read-mostly workloads and heavy batching where memory footprint is primary constraint.
  - Avoid aggressive quantization for safety-sensitive or highly factual models without human validation.

Regression triage playbook (step-by-step)
1) Detection:
   - Alert from comparison engine when any key metric crosses configured regression delta OR when canary job fails.
2) Initial triage (first 30 minutes):
   - Owner (model-owner oncall) acknowledges alert.
   - Snapshot: capture model version, prompt-set version, dataset manifest, harness config, and raw outputs.
   - Quick checks: run parallel quick-smoke (50 prompts) across baseline and new build to confirm regression.
3) Scope determination (30-120 minutes):
   - Is regression global or slice-specific? Use slice-level dashboards.
   - Check perf: did latency/resource changes coincide?
   - Check quantization: was a new quantized profile used? Re-run FP16 baseline if possible.
4) Root cause candidates:
   - Data drift / prompt set change (incorrect manifest or corrupted dataset).
   - Model change (new weights, architecture variant).
   - Quantization regression (precision loss).
   - Serving/runtime change (kernel mismatch, tokenizer difference, context truncation).
   - Upstream dependency (embedding encoder change, comparator metric update).
5) Remediation actions (ordered):
   - Hotfix revert to last-known-good model profile if rollout is in-progress.
   - If quantization implicated: switch to FP16 or less aggressive quantized profile.
   - If dataset corrupted: revert prompt manifest and re-run nightly job.
   - If runtime/kernel issue: pin kernel or apply targeted patch and re-run smoke tests.
6) Communication:
   - Post to #model-regressions channel with initial findings and rollback decision within 60 minutes.
   - If customer impact is suspected, notify Customer Success and include summary and ETA for fix.
7) Postmortem (within 7 days):
   - Owner writes a brief incident review covering cause, impact, detection path, mitigations, and a timeline.
   - Update model onboarding checklist or quantization profiles based on findings.

CI / automation examples
- Example minimal PR smoke job (YAML):

jobs:
  model-smoke-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'
      - name: Install deps
        run: pip install -r eval-harness/requirements.txt
      - name: Run smoke eval
        run: python eval-harness/run.py --model ${{ env.MODEL }} --prompt-set smoke --max-prompts 20 --output artifacts/smoke.json

- Example eval-harness config (JSON manifest snippet):

"manifest": "v1",
"id": "canonical-usage-v2",
"description": "Canonical production prompts for customer-facing assistant",
"sources": ["s3://redwood-evals/canonical/2027-06-01.jsonl"]

Owners, SLAs and contact points
- Eval harness owner: Applied ML team (primary: Priya Shenoy).
- Oncall for model regressions: model-owner rotation in Applied ML oncall rota.
- SLOs: nightly full-run completion 99% within window; PR smoke <5m pass rate 95% for healthy models.

Audit and compliance notes
- All eval runs are logged with immutable run IDs and artifacts stored for 90 days by default.
- For restricted models (privacy/compliance), datasets must be marked in the manifest with restricted=true and stored in customer-managed buckets where required.

Appendix: Quick triage checklist (one-page)
1) Acknowledge alert and snapshot run artifacts.
2) Run 50-prompt smoke against baseline and candidate.
3) Check quantization flag and revert if set.
4) Check dataset manifest integrity and prompt-set version.
5) Post preliminary status to #model-regressions and CS if customer facing.
6) Decide on rollback or targeted mitigation and execute.
